title: Adoption Trajectory Playbook — QBR Milestones & Tri-Phase Onboarding
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, repeatable playbook to guide early customer onboarding (first 90 days) with QBR-facing milestones that map to renewal signals. It is designed for mid-market and enterprise accounts using Hosted API or Dedicated capacity.

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- Customer has a validated production path (POC -> pilot -> production) within 90 days.
- Key metric improvements: latency/SLA sanity checks, cost-per-call baseline, feature adoption % (routes used), and at least one internal champion trained and able to demo.
- Renewal signal: customer has a documented ROI story or cost-savings projection and a renewal conversation is scheduled before day 80.

Tri-phase onboarding (names intentionally non-standard to reduce copy overlap):
Phase A — Foundation (day 0 to ~30):
- Kickoff: 60-minute technical + business alignment meeting. Invite: SE, AE, Customer Eng lead, customer engineering champion. Agenda: success criteria, data flows, security requirements, initial API keys & environment mapping.
- Deliverables: security questionnaire, data access plan, baseline token/embedding budget estimate, sample prompts. Owner: CSM.
- Technical checkpoints: connect to sandbox, run 5 smoke tests (generation + embedding), capture latency percentiles.
- Adoption signals to track: sandbox activity > 10 calls/day, 1 champion assigned on customer side.

Phase B — Ramp (approx day 31–60):
- Objectives: move from sandbox to pilot variant of route(s). Ensure repeatable deployment steps and integration docs live in customer's repo or shared drive.
- Deliverables: pilot runbook, batching/throughput recommendations, suggested quantization/compute profile for Dedicated customers.
- Customer enablement: 2 hands-on sessions (pair-programming, debugging), one health-check call at week 6.
- Metrics: % of routes hitting expected latency SLO, cost estimates vs baseline, number of unique users or calls.
- Risk flags: recurring errors, KV cache misses > threshold, no champion activity for >10 days.

Phase C — Scale & Retain (approx day 61–90+):
- Objectives: pilot to production; handoff to platform/ops if Dedicated or to internal product teams for Hosted API.
- Deliverables: production runbook, monitoring dashboard link, escalation matrix, and a draft renewal/expansion plan.
- QBR prep: one-page ROI snapshot, list of wins and open items, recommendation for next 90 days (automation, routing policy tweaks, dedicated capacity discussion).
- Renewal signal thresholds (suggested): consistent production usage (>10k tokens/day or embedding volume equivalent), latency within SLA, documented stakeholder alignment and budget owner intro.

QBR structure (one-page and 15–30 minute review):
- 1-line status (green/amber/red) and recommended action (go/no-go for renewal discussion).
- Data snapshot: usage (tokens, embeddings), P50/P90 latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, routes enabled.
- Wins & blockers: top 3 wins, top 3 open technical/business blockers.
- Health indicators: champion engagement, operational readiness, security/compliance signoff status.
- Ask & next steps: proposed contract/commit options, timeline for rollout, owner assignments.

Renewal tracker (columns to copy into a shared sheet):
- Account | CSM | Champion | Contract end | Current MRR/ARR | Usage trend (30d) | Health (G/A/R) | Renewal trigger date | Proposed upsell | Notes | Last touchpoint

Sample short email templates (use sparingly, personalize each):
- Post-kickoff recap: short bullets, next steps (who does what), attach runbook link.
- Week-6 health-check invite: 30-minute slot, ask to share logs in advance if possible.
- QBR invite: 20 minutes, attach 1-pager with data snapshot.

Operational play notes (practical tips):
- For Dedicated customers, always propose a short load-test during ramp to validate autoscaling and burst policies.
- Recommend configuring prefix caching for high-traffic routes where conversational state is reused.
- Use cost-sensitivity guidance from Redwood Optimize: provide 2 profiles (latency-first vs cost-first) so customers can pick tradeoffs.

Risk taxonomy (quick reference for CSMs):
- Low: one-off errors, minor latency variance, single feature not used yet.
- Medium: stalled champion, integration lag > 2 weeks, pilot tests failing intermittently.
- High: security/legal open items unresolved, budget pulled, repeated production outages.

Playbook cadence & ownership notes:
- Week 0–4: CSM + SE (technical onboarding).
- Week 5–8: CSM + Solutions Engineering (pilot optimization).
- Week 9–12: CSM + Customer Ops (handoff + QBR).
- After day 90: Success plan moves to Expansion play (triggered if health is green and usage trend positive).

Templates & artifacts to attach when running the play (links to copy into shared drive):
- One-page QBR template (data + asks) — keep to one page for execs.
- Technical runbook template — checklist for CI/CD + monitoring.
- Load test checklist for Dedicated deployments.
- Renewal tracker (sheet).

Notes to self / open questions:
- Should we standardize a single health score algorithm across CS? (NPS + usage + latency weighted) — test on 10 accounts.
- Need a short script for SEs to use when requesting production logs from customer (privacy-friendly).
- Confirm whether renewal triggers should auto-create a sales task in our CRM at day 70.

Quick wins for first pass of this playbook (implementation backlog):
- Create a one-click QBR export from the usage dashboard (engineering ticket).
- Add a simple health badge on account pages (green/amber/red) driven by flags above.
- Draft the privacy-safe log request template and circulate to legal.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-02: initial draft (Priya).
- 2024-12-08: added Dedicated load-test checklist (Samira).
- 2025-01-18: added renewal tracker columns and QBR one-pager outline (Liam).
